name: orbit
description: Action sub-agent for Olly Sentinel. Given a completed RCA enrichment, Orbit proposes exactly one action from a closed enum (troubleshoot, remediate_restart_service, no_action) as an action-proposal.v1 payload. It proposes; it never acts. On every inbound A2A message/send Orbit re-validates the COIN-minted AuthZ-CTX Olly carries, intersects the delegated permitted_actions with its own local grant (narrow-only: restart_service is capped 3 -> 1, and an action Orbit is not itself entitled to is refused before propose_action runs). Every proposal is then held in state 'proposed' until a human approves it with an ed25519-signed approval token that Orbit cannot mint, after which a deterministic executor performs the action under a separate write-entitled identity. This is the strategic decision from the design: Olly as a component with TROUBLESHOOT / REMEDIATE actions, reachable via Self-Healing or a direct authorized user request. A direct A2A message/send invokes propose_action and returns an input-required task that the signed approval resolves.

skills.name: Propose a remediation action
skills.description: Given a correlation-ID for a triaged incident, propose one action from the action-proposal.v1 closed enum and return it in state 'proposed'. The proposal requires human approval before execution: propose_action is gated by tool-confirmation, so a message/send comes back as an A2A input-required task that pauses until a decision. Approval is an ed25519-signed token bound to the specific proposal (proposal_id, correlation_id, action); Orbit holds only the public key and cannot approve its own proposals. Nothing runs until an approved proposal is executed by the deterministic executor under a separate write-entitled identity.

authz_ctx.name: X-AuthZ-CTX
authz_ctx.description: The COIN-minted AuthZ-CTX carried across the Olly -> Orbit A2A hop. Orbit verifies the HS256 signature and expiry against the shared secret, then intersects the inbound permitted_actions with its own local grant: it keeps only actions present in both and takes the lower limit (narrow-only, so restart_service drops from 3 to 1 and never widens). A message/send with no AuthZ-CTX is rejected with 401; a delegated action named in the companion X-AuthZ-Action header that does not survive narrowing is rejected with 403. The same authz_ctx_id flows across the hop and is echoed as X-AuthZ-CTX-Id on the response, so one id anchors the whole chain for audit. This is the one A2A auth scheme the replica actually enforces at the endpoint.

eems.description: EEMS-issued bearer identifying the caller. Orbit itself holds the read-only gco-sentinel-read role and no write entitlement; the executor runs under a separate write-entitled identity. In the ARC estate this bearer resolves to the caller's COIN M2M credential (the AuthZ-CTX above is that credential as it arrives from Olly).

approval_jwt.description: An ed25519-signed approval token (EdDSA JWT) authorizing a specific proposal to move proposed -> approved -> executed. Minted by the approval service, which holds the private key; Orbit verifies with the public key only and cannot mint one. Claims bind the token to one proposal_id, correlation_id, and action, so it cannot be replayed onto another proposal.
